stories.title: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017
stories.blurb: DeepSeek drops another Flash-series model, and the HN discussion is on fire with 667 comments. If you're integrating LLMs into workflows or evaluating alternatives to Claude/GPT, this is a must-benchmark — Flash models are optimized for speed and cost without sacrificing too much quality.

stories.title: DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests
stories.blurb: DeepSeek now offers a web search-and-fetch API at $0.75/1k successful requests — meaningfully cheaper than Bing or Brave Search for LLM-augmented pipelines. If you're building retrieval-augmented tools or AI agents that browse the web, this pricing changes the calculus significantly.

stories.title: Show HN: Sphinx – A hook that quizzes you on your AI's code before shipping
stories.blurb: Sphinx is a pre-commit hook that asks you targeted questions about the AI-generated code you're about to ship — forcing you to actually understand it. A clever antidote to blindly committing Claude Code output; exactly the kind of guardrail that responsible AI-assisted dev should have.

stories.title: Codex Desktop continuously generates Crashpad pending dumps
stories.blurb: OpenAI's Codex Desktop app is silently flooding users' disks with Crashpad dumps — a real concern for anyone running it on a Mac. If you've noticed unexplained disk usage, this thread explains why and tracks the fix. Good reminder to audit what your AI tooling is quietly doing in the background.

stories.title: Pele – Mermaid diagrams as themeable SVG
stories.blurb: Pele renders Mermaid diagram syntax into clean, fully themeable SVGs — no browser, no runtime. Perfect for dropping architecture diagrams into documentation, Obsidian notes, or Angular component docs. The theming story is what makes this special compared to the stock Mermaid renderer.

stories.title: NY announces game ownership bill requiring ownership rather than licensing
stories.blurb: New York is moving to require that digital game sales convey actual ownership — not just a revocable license — and mandate publishers keep games functional after support ends. If this passes it sets a precedent that could ripple into software licensing broadly, including SaaS and app stores.

stories.title: Bleached corals thrive within days when touching healthy neighbour
stories.blurb: Stressed, bleached corals recover dramatically within days simply by being in physical contact with healthy neighbors — a discovery that upends assumptions about coral resilience. The mechanism is still being decoded but it hints at coral reef restoration strategies that don't require growing new coral from scratch.

stories.title: Solar surpasses nuclear power globally for first time
stories.blurb: For the first time in history, solar energy generation has overtaken nuclear globally — a milestone that seemed far-fetched a decade ago. The HN comments dig into the nuances of capacity vs. generation vs. reliability, making this a rich thread for understanding where the energy transition actually stands.

stories.title: Making chicken transparent using Dorito dust
stories.blurb: A physicist walks through how matching the refractive index of tissue with Dorito seasoning oil renders chicken visually transparent — legitimately. It's a playful application of the same optical clearing techniques used in biological imaging research, explained with rare clarity.

stories.title: How employment is changing at Anthropic
stories.blurb: Anthropic publishes a candid look at how their own workforce is shifting as AI capabilities grow — what roles are expanding, shrinking, and transforming. Essential reading if you're thinking about how AI tools like Claude Code are reshaping the developer labor market from the inside out.

stories.title: Backdooring Open-Weight AI Models: "Abliteration is a cheap fine-tune that takes away a model's ability to refuse."
stories.blurb: Bruce Schneier covers a chilling attack: abliteration fine-tunes strip an open-weight model's refusals, then a poisoned model exfiltrates credentials on a trigger word — demonstrated live against Codex. If you're using local or open-weight models in any pipeline, this threat model is now real and needs to be in your security thinking.

stories.title: An Israeli firm is sending spyware through online ads, researchers say | The Verge
stories.blurb: Researchers have caught an Israeli surveillance firm delivering zero-click spyware payloads through ordinary online ads — no interaction required. This is particularly relevant for the Apple ecosystem, where ad-delivered exploits have historically been a primary vector for sophisticated commercial spyware.

stories.title: TrellisWM · The fractal window manager for Mac
stories.blurb: TrellisWM is a new macOS window manager built around a fractal tiling metaphor — windows nest and split recursively rather than snapping to a fixed grid. For keyboard-driven developers juggling Claude Code, a terminal, and a browser, this is a genuinely different approach to screen real estate worth trying.

stories.title: Drafts Adds a Chat Console and Better Dictation - MacSparky
stories.blurb: Drafts — the beloved iOS/macOS capture-first writing app — ships a chat console and improved dictation in its latest update. For Obsidian users who also use Drafts as a quick-capture inbox, the AI chat integration brings LLM assistance directly into your writing workflow without leaving the app.

stories.title: Ioskeley Mono
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: font, monospace, opensource
stories.blurb: Ioskeley Mono is a free, open-source monospace font that captures Berkeley Mono's aesthetic by configuring Iosevka — three widths, ten weights, italics, and full Nerd Font support. If you've been eyeing Berkeley Mono but balk at the price, this is a serious, high-quality alternative to drop into your editor today.

stories.title: GitHub - morluto/rea: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: morluto, ghidra, hopper, mcp, reverse-engineering, binary-analysis
stories.blurb: REA is an open-source tool that wires AI agents to Ghidra and Hopper to automate reverse engineering of native binaries and app behavior — exposing an MCP interface for agent orchestration. For security researchers or developers curious about what's inside closed-source components, this dramatically lowers the barrier to automated binary analysis.

stories.title: The RSS Universe — Readers, Tools & Standards
stories.blurb: A comprehensive, opinionated map of the entire RSS ecosystem — readers, feed generators, monitoring tools, directories, and the underlying standards. No algorithm, no engagement bait: this is the antidote to doom-scrolling, and a useful reference if you're building anything feed-powered.

stories.title: Shotcandy — make your screenshots look lovely
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: 截图美化
stories.blurb: Shotcandy wraps screenshots in beautiful backgrounds and frames entirely in-browser — free, open source, no account needed. A dead-simple tool for making your CLI outputs, Xcode screenshots, or demo recordings look polished before sharing them with your team or posting publicly.

stories.title: Time's up for the leap second as scientists swap it for the leap hour | Science | The Guardian
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: funny, science, time, history, measurement, computers, programming, standards
stories.blurb: Scientists have officially retired the leap second — the bane of distributed systems engineers everywhere — replacing it with a leap hour that won't occur for centuries. A landmark moment for computing infrastructure: the edge case that caused countless production incidents is finally being abolished.

stories.title: GitHub - chenxiachan/textfold: Fold papers, web pages, files, and AI replies into five levels of detail.
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: zotero, llm, ai
stories.blurb: Textfold progressively collapses any document — paper, webpage, AI response — into five zoom levels from overview to full text. For researchers and developers drowning in long LLM outputs or dense documentation, this is a genuinely new interaction model for reading and navigating text.
